title: Knee Extensors Endurance Test with Elastic Resistance
author: Jéssica irsch Micheletti
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kcmcsu6

steps.title: Record participant anthropometrics
steps.instruction: Measure each participant’s body mass using a Tanita BC‑554 scale (Iron Man/Inner, Illinois, USA) and height using a Sany stadiometer (American Medical do Brasil, São Paulo, Brazil).

steps.title: Perform initial easy‑load sets
steps.instruction: Have participants execute two consecutive 20‑second knee‑extensor extension sets using an individual load classified as “easy” (2 points) on the OMNI‑RES scale.

steps.title: Execute extensions with intermediate resistances
steps.instruction: Using the six resistance configurations shown in Chart 1, have participants perform one 20‑second extension set for each configuration employing two intermediate resistance levels.

substeps.instruction: Select first resistance configuration and perform a 20‑second set.
Select second resistance configuration and perform a 20‑second set.
Continue sequentially through all six configurations.

steps.title: Stage 3 simulation sessions
steps.instruction: Conduct two simulation sessions to familiarize participants and verify the appropriate resistance:

substeps.instruction: Start with a 100 cm elastic tube (9 mm × 6 mm diameter) as shown in Chart 1.
Keep both the physical therapist and the participant blinded to the resistance used.
An independent research assistant stores data and adjusts the tube distance as needed.

steps.title: Perform final functional resistance test
steps.instruction: Have participants perform the functional resistance test (FRT) using the pre‑defined load determined in Stage 3.

substeps.instruction: Execute the FRT with the selected load.
An independent research assistant records time and repetitions.
Do not reveal the test results (time and repetitions) to the participant.
